Current evidence / state: All 36 Muslingo Tajwid lessons cite one Understand Al-Quran course URL; that provider's terms prohibit copying/reproduction without written permission.
Risk to learner or launch: High legal and launch risk; unclear whether explanations, examples or assessment wording are derivative.
Concrete action: Either secure a written commercial curriculum license, or independently re-author all lessons from rule-level facts with new examples, scripts, exercises and assessments.
Acceptance evidence: Signed license, or clean-room authoring log plus side-by-side originality review and rights sign-off.

Current evidence / state: No named Tajwid/Qira'at editorial board, reviewer credentials, approval date or correction policy found in the current course inventory.
Risk to learner or launch: Users cannot distinguish product content from scholar-approved instruction; errors may persist.
Concrete action: Appoint a lead reviewer holding recognized ijazah in Hafs 'an 'Asim, a second reviewer, and an Arabic/ru/kk terminology editor; publish the governance policy.
Acceptance evidence: Reviewer roster, credentials verified, signed approval per release, versioned correction register.

Current evidence / state: Current reader pulls Arabic editions from AlQuran.cloud while Muslingo has no visible source/version/checksum registry in the audited content inventory.
Risk to learner or launch: Silent upstream changes or edition mixing can create integrity defects.
Concrete action: Select one canonical Hafs text package (KFGQPC or Tanzil), store version and SHA-256, prohibit mutation, and compare every API response/build artifact against it.
Acceptance evidence: 6236-ayah count, source version, checksum, basmala/numbering policy, automated diff test and zero unexplained differences.

Current evidence / state: Muslingo requests ru.kuliev and transliteration via AlQuran.cloud; edition-level rights, version and correction ownership are not documented in-product.
Risk to learner or launch: Aggregator terms may not cover the underlying translation; outdated or corrected translations may remain cached.
Concrete action: Build a translation registry; prefer QuranEnc editions with publisher/version/attribution; obtain confirmation for Kuliev and any transliteration.
Acceptance evidence: Per-edition rights field, version/date, attribution string, update job and takedown contact.

Current evidence / state: Current code combines AlQuran.cloud per-ayah audio and MP3Quran surah audio without a recording-level rights ledger.
Risk to learner or launch: Reciter estates or hosts may restrict commercial/offline redistribution or request removal.
Concrete action: Use KFGQPC approved recordings for the core pack; register every reciter/riwayah/file source, grant, checksum and removal path.
Acceptance evidence: Recording inventory with archived license evidence, attribution, offline/stream permission and tested replacement procedure.

Current evidence / state: 36 Tajwid lessons reference only 19 unique ayahs in the current inventory.
Risk to learner or launch: Learners may memorize examples rather than generalize rules to unseen Quran text.
Concrete action: Create a rule-to-example matrix with multiple positive, contrastive and unseen examples per rule; balance positions within words/ayahs.
Acceptance evidence: At least 6 reviewed examples per core rule, 2 contrastive non-examples, and an unseen assessment set with no lesson leakage.

Current evidence / state: Muslingo has speech evaluation, but the audited product evidence does not establish phoneme-, makhraj- or Tajwid-rule-level validation.
Risk to learner or launch: Calling generic ASR similarity a Tajwid score may misteach learners and overstate accuracy.
Concrete action: Separate four scores: recall/completeness, word accuracy, pronunciation, and Tajwid application. Ship only validated dimensions; route uncertain cases to a teacher.
Acceptance evidence: Published evaluation spec, Arabic recitation test set, per-dimension precision/recall, confidence threshold and human escalation.

Current evidence / state: Hafiz mode and due reviews exist, but no transparent Sabaq/Sabqi/Manzil or adaptive-interval model is documented in the content inventory.
Risk to learner or launch: Review load may be arbitrary; long-term retention cannot be explained or coached.
Concrete action: Expose a configurable new/recent/old review model, adaptive intervals and teacher overrides; start with Juz 30 and prayer-surah pathways.
Acceptance evidence: Learner-visible daily plan, interval rules, override log, retention metric and 4-week pilot results.

Current evidence / state: No teacher-validated checkpoints, sanad/ijazah pathway or cumulative oral exam flow found.
Risk to learner or launch: Automation alone cannot certify recitation or advanced memorization.
Concrete action: Add periodic recorded submissions and optional live/async review through qualified partners; label product certificates as completion, not ijazah.
Acceptance evidence: Reviewer SLA, rubric, consent/retention policy, pass record and explicit certificate wording.

Current evidence / state: No dedicated similar-ayah/confusable-passage drills found, despite 602 unique ayahs in Quran lessons.
Risk to learner or launch: Advanced learners may plateau on common substitution errors.
Concrete action: Create scholar-reviewed mutashabihat sets using QUL only after dataset-specific license clearance, or author the set internally.
Acceptance evidence: Rights-approved dataset, reviewed pairs/groups, spaced drills and error analytics.

Current evidence / state: Current titles cover core makharij, nun/mim, madd, lam/ra and basic waqf, but no auditable mastery map exists.
Risk to learner or launch: Important applied skills may be shallow or absent even when topics are named.
Concrete action: Publish a mastery map including lahn jali/khafi, connected reading/hamzat al-wasl, silent-letter conventions, waqf/ibtida decisions, applied full-surah capstones and any intentionally excluded advanced qira'at topics.
Acceptance evidence: Signed scope matrix with prerequisites, examples, assessment type and level boundary for every objective.

Current evidence / state: One generic Tajwid route is visible; no diagnostic placement or age/fluency route found.
Risk to learner or launch: Beginners are overwhelmed and fluent readers repeat material; children and adults need different pacing/safeguards.
Concrete action: Create placement checks for script decoding, fluency, makharij and core rules; branch into beginner, fluent-correction and hifz-support routes.
Acceptance evidence: Validated placement rubric, misplacement audit and age-appropriate learning variants.

Current evidence / state: Muslingo serves English/Russian/Kazakh, while the cited Tajwid source is English/Urdu and there is no documented bilingual scholarly review.
Risk to learner or launch: Literal translation can distort technical terms and examples.
Concrete action: Create a controlled Arabic–English–Russian–Kazakh glossary; require separate subject-matter review of ru and kk scripts and voice-over.
Acceptance evidence: Approved glossary, reviewer sign-off, back-translation sampling and zero unresolved terminology flags.

Current evidence / state: Official channels are useful, but public viewing is being considered alongside owned lessons.
Risk to learner or launch: Downloading, clipping, transcribing or repackaging videos can breach YouTube and creator terms.
Concrete action: Use optional outbound links or official embeds only; store channel/video URL and attribution; request written rights before any derivative use.
Acceptance evidence: No downloaded media in build; embed/link QA; permission record for every adapted asset.

Current evidence / state: Record-from-memory and speech evaluation process learner recitation; no content-level governance evidence covers consent, retention or minors.
Risk to learner or launch: Sensitive voice data may be retained or reused beyond learner expectations.
Concrete action: Adopt explicit consent, shortest practical retention, deletion/export, no model training without opt-in, minor/guardian controls and regional data review.
Acceptance evidence: Data map, retention schedule, delete test, consent copy, vendor DPA and minor flow QA.

Current evidence / state: No audited specification for slow/mu'allim audio, color-independent Tajwid cues, keyboard/screen-reader paths or hearing/vision needs.
Risk to learner or launch: Learners with disabilities or low fluency may be excluded; color-only rules are inaccessible.
Concrete action: Add adjustable speed where licensed, ayah/word loops, text labels alongside colors, scalable Quran font, transcripts/instructions and screen-reader testing.
Acceptance evidence: WCAG-oriented QA, color-independent rule labels, audio controls and assistive-technology test record.

Current evidence / state: External APIs and curricula can change; current materials lack a visible refresh cadence and correction intake.
Risk to learner or launch: Licenses, versions and corrections can drift after launch.
Concrete action: Maintain a source register with owner, last checked, next review, checksum/version and correction/takedown SLA; sync Quran Foundation content at its required cadence when used.
Acceptance evidence: Quarterly rights review, automated version alerts, weekly eligible content sync and correction log.

Current evidence / state: Completion counts exist, but mastery definitions for recall, word accuracy, pronunciation and rule application are not separated.
Risk to learner or launch: Progress dashboards can reward activity without verified learning.
Concrete action: Define mastery thresholds per objective, cumulative retention checks, calibration against human raters and confidence-aware reporting.
Acceptance evidence: Metric dictionary, inter-rater agreement, holdout results and dashboard labels that match evidence.

Current evidence / state: Live/async human review is recommended, but no safeguarding workflow is documented for minors or gender preferences.
Risk to learner or launch: Partnership expansion can create safety, privacy and trust risks.
Concrete action: Require verified teachers, same-gender option, guardian consent, moderated communications, reporting/escalation and no off-platform contact.
Acceptance evidence: Safeguarding policy, background/credential checks where lawful, audit logs and incident drill.

Current evidence / state: The app contains 246 lessons and 2664 steps, but source coverage differs sharply: Quran 11.0%, Arabic 83.2%, Tajwid 100%, Rules 9.1% in the local inventory.
Risk to learner or launch: A URL field alone may be mistaken for rights clearance or scholarly approval; gaps can remain hidden.
Concrete action: Replace binary 'sourced' status with provenance states: canonical data, factual reference, licensed adaptation, internally authored/reviewed, and unresolved.
Acceptance evidence: Every lesson/asset has author, sources, rights basis, reviewer, version and release status; unresolved items fail the release gate.
